messages.author: 95823b040dda7f6f
messages.subject: Package location with user_apps
parts:
Hi Josh,

I know there have been questions about this before, but I can't get it to work.

I'm using RStudio (versions/system below) with a new install of Shiny today. RStudio and Shiny are working great. This is on Amazon EC2.

I'm trying to run a shiny app from a user account. I have /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf as:
run_as shiny;

server {
  listen 3838;

  location / {
    site_dir /var/shiny-server/www;
    log_dir /var/shiny-server/log;
    directory_index on;
  }

  location / {
    user_apps on;
  }
}

This is working fine and I can see my app at http://<server>:3838/<user>/<app>/

The problem is making packages available to this. The user packages aren't available as it is being run as user = shiny. I've tried various permutations of added paths including in rserver.config without success. I've even (and I know I shouldn't probably do this) made "shiny" a normal user and added the packages to that account, but that still doesn't work.

Would it be possible to have an option that when user_apps = on, the packages for that user are available to shiny?

Is there a line I can add some where to make this happen? I'm not that au fait with linux paths and all the jazz.

Error is:

An error has occurred

The application failed to start.

The application exited during initialization.

Error in library(ggplot2) : there is no package called ‘ggplot2’ Calls: runApp ... eval -> source -> withVisible -> eval -> eval -> library Execution halted


Did you say some where else that ggplot2 had been added to a system library? I can't find it.

Many thanks!

Ewen

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Package location with user_apps
parts:
To install R packages in the system-wide library, you can run:

sudo su - -c "R -e \"install.packages('shiny', repos='http://cran.rstudio.com/')\""

and replace 'shiny' with the package(s) you want to install.
